did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hezekiah received a difficult message from the prophet Isaiah: he was to put his affairs in order because he was about to die and would not recover.
Did you know? After hearing the message, Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord.
Did you know? In his prayer, Hezekiah recalled his faithfulness to the Lord and his good deeds, and he wept bitterly.
Did you know? The Lord heard Hezekiah’s prayer and saw his tears. He promised to heal him, and Hezekiah would go up to the house of the Lord on the third day.
Did you know? In addition to healing him, the Lord promised Hezekiah fifteen more years of life and protection for Jerusalem from the king of Assyria.
Did you know? Isaiah ordered that a cake of figs be placed on Hezekiah’s boil, and afterward the Scripture says, “And he recovered.”
Did you know? Hezekiah asked for a sign that he would be healed and go up to the house of the Lord on the third day; he was not satisfied with only a promise.
Did you know? The sign given to Hezekiah involved a change in the movement of the shadow: the shadow would move forward ten steps or go back ten steps.
Did you know? In response to Isaiah’s prayer, the shadow went back up the steps on which it had descended—ten steps backward.

Did you know? Hezekiah showed the Babylonian envoys all his treasures: silver, gold, spices, fine oil, and everything found in his treasuries. The Scripture emphasizes that there was nothing he did not show them.
